# Independent audit: C15 on ten vertices disproves the general symmetry conjecture

**Verdict: VERIFIED, with an elementary all-types proof and an independent exact checker.** For H generated by (0 1 2)(3 4 5 6 7), fixing 8 and 9,

    tau_T(H)=32,     tau_E(H)=31.

Here tau counts isomorphism types whose automorphism group contains an S10-conjugate of H; E means Royle-sign-even graphs. This is an explicit counterexample at n=10, **not a claim of least possible order**. It refutes general odd-order HYP-9340(a). The theorem for odd p-groups and its one-prime Sylow-action bijection remain valid.

The checker was written independently, without reading or importing the producer's code. It constructs all 512 labelled H-fixed tournaments and all 512 labelled H-fixed graphs. The 64 figures below are reduced presentations, not labelled fixed-point counts.

## 1. Fixed objects and coverage

Write A={0,1,2}, B={3,4,5,6,7}, c=8, d=9. Powers of the displayed generator give the separate 3- and 5-cycles, so H is C3 times C5 in this action. It has nine orbits on unordered vertex pairs: one inside A, two inside B, and one for each of the six pairs of blocks A,B,{c},{d}. On the last six orbits, adjacency or orientation is uniform.

Every type admitting a conjugate of H can be relabelled to be fixed by this exact H. Consequently enumeration of the H-fixed objects covers every type counted by tau; the only remaining issue is quotienting by **all** isomorphisms, not merely by a normalizer.

## 2. Tournament count: exactly 32 actual types

Inside A there are two directed triangles. Inside B there are four circulant tournaments: choose one element from each of {1,-1},{2,-2} in F5. Multiplication by F5's four nonzero elements is transitive on these four choices. Internal relabellings therefore normalize A to one C3 and B to one regular five-vertex tournament R5, without changing any between-block orientation. All H-fixed tournament types are represented among the 2^6=64 arbitrary oriented quotients on the four blocks.

### Why no hidden isomorphism merges different quotient types

A module of a tournament is a vertex subset seen uniformly by every outside vertex. A strongly connected module is a **strong module**: it cannot overlap another module without containment. To see this, let modules M,N have all three of M\N, M intersection N, N\M nonempty. Fix z in N\M. Its uniform relation to M, combined with each x in M\N seeing N uniformly, forces every edge between M\N and M intersection N to point in the same direction. Thus M has a nontrivial directed cut and is not strongly connected.

Both A and B are strongly connected modules. C3 is prime. R5 is prime as well: a two-vertex module would make its two outdegrees differ by one, contradicting regularity; a module of size three or four would force an outside vertex to have outdegree in {0,1,3,4}, again contradicting degree two.

The C3 module A is unique. Any other strongly connected three-vertex module is nested with or disjoint from each of A and B. It cannot be a proper module of prime B, cannot properly overlap A, and cannot fit in the two singleton vertices. A different prime strongly connected five-vertex module is likewise impossible: if disjoint from B it must be A union {c,d}, which contains the nontrivial module A and is not prime. Therefore B is unique too.

Every tournament isomorphism preserves A and B and may only exchange the singleton vertices c,d at the quotient level. That exchange acts freely on the 64 quotient tournaments because it reverses the c-d arc. Hence there are exactly 64/2=32 actual tournament types. The checker independently tests uniqueness of these modules in every one of the 64 presentations.

## 3. Graph reduction: 448 fixed graphs are automatically odd

Inside A an H-fixed graph is empty or K3. Inside B it is empty, C5, its complementary C5, or K5. Every nonempty option is sign-odd:

- a transposition is odd on K3 or K5;
- the reflection x->-x is odd on either five-cycle presentation, reversing exactly one of its two swapped antipodal pairs that are edges.

Since outside vertices see an entire block uniformly, these block automorphisms extend to automorphisms of the whole graph with the same orientation sign. One may orient all crossing edges uniformly by blocks to see that the extension adds no reversed crossing edges; orientation independence then removes this chosen orientation.

Thus seven of the eight internal patterns are odd for all 64 external patterns, excluding 448 graphs. All possible even types occur among the 64 blowups with independent blocks A and B, of sizes 3 and 5, and the two singletons.

## 4. Exact all-isomorphism and sign analysis of the 64 blowups

Two vertices are false twins when their open neighborhoods are equal. False-twin classes are intrinsic independent sets; the quotient graph, marked with their sizes, reconstructs the original graph. Every automorphism permutes these weighted classes, then independently permutes vertices inside each class. An internal permutation has sign +1: it is generated by transpositions of nonadjacent false twins, each of which reverses an even number of edges.

Initially A and B lie inside false-twin classes, which may also absorb some of c,d or merge with each other. The resulting weighted quotient determines the six-edge four-block presentation up to exchanging c,d:

- If A and B remain in different false-twin classes, their sizes are 3+r and 5+s, where r+s<=2. Unless both sizes are five, the B-class is the unique largest class and the A-class is the unique other class of size at least three. Any remaining classes contain only the singleton vertices. Assigning a singleton to a block's false-twin class does not create another quotient presentation, since all such vertices have identical adjacency.
- If the A- and B-classes merge, their common class has size at least eight and is uniquely identified; the remaining information again consists only of the singleton vertices up to exchange.
- The only equal-large-class exception is size five plus five, with A,c,d merged on one side and B on the other. Distinct false-twin classes in this two-class case must be adjacent, so the graph is K5,5. Interchanging its two sides produces the same four-block adjacency pattern, not a second type.

Thus the 64 presentations have exactly the orbits under the singleton exchange. There are 16 fixed presentations: c and d have identical adjacency to A and to B, while the A-B and c-d edges are free. Hence Burnside gives (64+16)/2=40 actual graph types.

### All odd automorphisms

In all weighted twin quotients except the two-five-class case, the only possible nontrivial class permutation exchanges the two singleton classes. If they have the same adjacency to A and B and are adjacent, their transposition is odd. There are exactly

    2 choices for A-B times 2 for their common A-adjacency
      times 2 for their common B-adjacency =8

such presentations, each fixed by the singleton exchange and hence a distinct type. If the singleton vertices are nonadjacent with equal external neighborhoods, they belong to one false-twin class and swapping them is even.

The equal-five-class exception contributes one additional odd type: K5,5. Swapping its two sides pairs the ten vertices into five adjacent pairs and has sign (-1)^5=-1. All internal permutations within its independent sides are even. It is distinct from the eight singleton-twin odd types.

There are no other possible weighted-class permutations. Therefore exactly 40-8-1=31 of the types are globally sign-even.

## 5. The missed coordinate in the inherited conjecture

The graph K5,5 is even relative to the normalizer N_S10(H), but globally odd. Its two sides are B and A union {c,d}. Every normalizer element preserves H-orbit sizes, so it preserves B and the other side; its allowed within-side actions are sign-even. The globally odd side swap does not normalize H, since it sends H's five-point orbit to a set consisting of an H three-point orbit and two fixed points.

After excluding the eight normalizer-odd singleton-swap types, there are 32 normalizer-even graph types, matching the 32 tournament types as expected. But the one globally odd K5,5 type survives that normalizer test. Here it is not cancelled by tournament orbit multiplicity: the unique C3 and R5 modules prove multiplicity one. This precisely explains the defect 32-31=1.

## 6. Reproduction and exact witnesses

    python3 -B independent_c15.py
    python3 -B -O independent_c15.py

`independent_c15.json` contains every remaining graph's quotient mask, false-twin sizes, full automorphism order, global and normalizer-even status, and a concrete odd permutation when needed. It also records the full fixed universes, 448 explicit internal-odd exclusions, all 64 tournament module checks, and the K5,5 edge list. Its four-block quotient mask is 25 in low-bit order AB,Ac,Ad,Bc,Bd,cd, namely edges AB,Bc,Bd.

This independent path uses neither the producer's graph canonicalizer nor its tournament isomorphism routine. Its graph classification is exact via weighted false-twin quotients; tournament classification is certified by the unique-module argument and exhaustive module checks. There is no heuristic graph-isomorphism filter or sampled universe.
